entry: Russian-American poet and essayist. Born in Leningrad (now [[Saint Petersburg|Saint Petersburg]]) into a Jewish family, he survived the [[Siege of Leningrad|Siege of Leningrad]] as a child and later taught himself Polish and English so he could translate poets such as Czesław Miłosz and John Donne. Brodsky ran afoul of Soviet authorities and was expelled from the [[Soviet Union|Soviet Union]] in 1972, settling in the United States with the help of W. H. Auden. He taught at Mount Holyoke College and at universities including Yale, Columbia and Michigan. He won the [[Nobel Prize|Nobel Prize]] in Literature in 1987 "for an all-embracing authorship, imbued with clarity of thought and poetic intensity" and was appointed United States Poet Laureate in 1991. Viktor Krivulin said that Brodsky was a Christian poet, and Brodsky himself said in 1972, "I consider myself a Christian. Not a good one but I try to be."

Polish-British novelist and story writer. Born in Berdychiv, then part of the [[Russian Empire|Russian Empire]], to Polish parents, Conrad did not speak English fluently until his twenties, yet became a master prose stylist in that language. He drew on his years in the French and British merchant navies for novels and stories, many set at sea, that depicted crises of human individuality in what he saw as an indifferent and amoral world. Writing near the peak of the [[British Empire|British Empire]], he treated imperialism and colonialism in works such as *Heart of Darkness* and *Lord Jim*. Critics have called him a literary impressionist and an early modernist, and many films have been adapted from his fiction.

English botanist and explorer. A founder of geographical botany, Hooker was [[Charles Darwin|Charles Darwin]]'s closest friend and his primary scientific confidant. He trained as a surgeon at the University of Glasgow and joined an Antarctic expedition as assistant surgeon, collecting and describing plants in the Falkland Islands and Tierra del Fuego. Later expeditions to the [[Himalayas|Himalayas]] and [[Sikkim|Sikkim]] yielded numerous rhododendron species. He served for 20 years as director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, succeeding his father, William Jackson Hooker. He reviewed the manuscript of *On the Origin of Species* and, with [[Charles Lyell|Charles Lyell]], arranged the 1858 joint presentation of Darwin's and [[Alfred Russel Wallace|Alfred Russel Wallace]]'s papers on natural selection. He received the highest honors of British science.

French mathematician and physicist. Born in Auxerre, the son of a tailor, Fourier was orphaned at nine and educated by the Benedictines. He was imprisoned briefly during the Terror, then taught at the École Polytechnique. He accompanied Napoleon to Egypt in 1798 as scientific adviser and was later appointed prefect of the Isère department at Grenoble, where he began experiments on the propagation of heat. His 1822 treatise *Théorie analytique de la chaleur* showed that arbitrary functions could be represented as infinite sums of sine and cosine terms. This work initiated the study of [[Fourier series|Fourier series]], which developed into [[Fourier analysis|Fourier analysis]] and applications to [[Heat transfer|heat transfer]]. The [[Fourier transform|Fourier transform]] is named in his honor. He is generally credited with the discovery of the [[Greenhouse effect|greenhouse effect]].

Biblical figure, eleventh son of Jacob and firstborn of Rachel. Joseph was a dream interpreter and an important figure in the [[Book of Genesis|Book of Genesis]]. His envious brothers sold him into slavery in Egypt, where he was imprisoned after rising in the household of Potiphar. After correctly interpreting Pharaoh's dreams, he became second-in-command in Egypt and saved the country during a famine. Through him, Jacob's family was allowed to settle in the Land of Goshen in the eastern Nile Delta. In Jewish tradition he is the ancestor of a second Messiah, Mashiach ben Yosef. Christian tradition often reads him as a precursor to [[Jesus|Jesus]], and in [[Islam|Islam]] he is regarded as a prophet.

German Nazi politician and propagandist. Born in Rheydt, Goebbels earned a doctorate in philology at Heidelberg, joined the Nazi Party in 1924 and became Gauleiter of Berlin in 1926. As Reich Minister of Propaganda from 1933, he gained control over the news, media, arts and flow of information in Nazi Germany, making particularly effective use of radio and film. His ministry promoted antisemitism, and he advocated the extermination of Jews in the [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]]. In 1943 he pressed for "total war", and in 1944 [[Adolf Hitler|Adolf Hitler]] appointed him Reich Plenipotentiary for Total War. After Hitler's death he served one day as Chancellor of Germany. He then died by [[Suicide|suicide]] with his wife, Magda, after poisoning their six children with cyanide.

Austrian composer of the [[Classical period (music)|Classical period]]. Haydn rose from humble origins, first as a chorister at St. Stephen's Cathedral in Vienna and then as a freelance musician. He spent much of his working life as music director for the Esterházy family at Eszterháza in Hungary, where isolation from other composers forced him to become original. He was pivotal in the evolution of [[Chamber music|chamber music]] forms such as the string quartet and piano trio, and is called the "Father of the [[Symphony|Symphony]]" and "Father of Sonata Form". After the death of his patron Nikolaus Esterházy in 1790, he traveled to London and Vienna. His late oratorios *The Creation* (1798) and *The Seasons* (1801) were widely admired. He taught Beethoven and was the elder brother of Michael Haydn.

Holy Roman Emperor (r. 1765–1790) and sole ruler of the Habsburg monarchy from 1780. The eldest son of [[Maria Theresa|Maria Theresa]], Joseph pursued enlightened absolutism, with reforms that secularized, liberalized and modernized the state. Opposition blocked full implementation of his programs, and his foreign policy isolated Austria despite some territorial gains. He is ranked with [[Catherine the Great|Catherine the Great]] and [[Frederick the Great|Frederick the Great]] as one of the three great Enlightenment monarchs. His policies are known as Josephinism. He supported composers including [[Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart|Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart]] and Antonio Salieri. He died without a known surviving legitimate heir and was succeeded by his brother Leopold II.

English surgeon and pioneer of antiseptic surgery. At the Glasgow Royal Infirmary, Lister introduced carbolic acid (modern-day [[Phenol|phenol]]) to sterilize instruments, skin, sutures, hands and wards. Drawing on [[Louis Pasteur|Louis Pasteur]]'s germ theory of fermentation, he recognized that putrefaction in wounds is caused by germs. His antiseptic system reduced post-operative [[Infection|infection]] and, by his account, cut amputation mortality from 45% to 15%. His research on inflammation, microscopy and surgical survival also advanced medicine. He was appointed Regius Professor of Surgery at Glasgow in 1860, was elevated to the peerage as Baron Lister in 1897, and served as president of the Royal Society from 1895 to 1900. He is known as the "father of modern surgery".

French chemist and physicist. With [[Alexander von Humboldt|Alexander von Humboldt]], he discovered that water is formed of two parts hydrogen and one part oxygen by volume. He also formulated a law stating that at constant pressure the volume of a gas increases in proportion to its absolute temperature; the law is usually called Charles's law, though some sources use his name. He co-discovered [[Boron|boron]] in 1808 and isolated [[Iodine|iodine]]. In 1804 he made a hydrogen-balloon ascent to 7,016 meters (23,018 ft), used to study the atmosphere. His work on alcohol–water mixtures led to the degrees Gay-Lussac, used to measure alcoholic beverages in many countries. He succeeded Antoine François Fourcroy as professor of chemistry at the École Polytechnique.

Italian-born French mathematician and astronomer. In 1766 he succeeded [[Leonhard Euler|Leonhard Euler]] as director of mathematics at the Prussian Academy of Sciences in Berlin, where he stayed for over twenty years. His treatise *Mécanique analytique* (1788) offered the most comprehensive treatment of classical mechanics since Isaac Newton and led to [[Lagrangian mechanics|Lagrangian mechanics]]. He was one of the creators of the calculus of variations and developed the method of [[Lagrange multiplier|Lagrange multipliers]]. He proved that every natural number is a sum of four squares. His study of the [[Three-body problem|three-body problem]] identified the special solutions known as [[Lagrange point|Lagrangian points]]. He became the first professor of analysis at the École Polytechnique in 1794.

American Republican senator from Wisconsin, 1947 until his death. In February 1950 McCarthy rose to national fame by claiming to have a list of communists employed in the State Department. He alleged Communist infiltration of the federal government, the military, universities and the film industry. The Senate censured him in 1954 by a vote of 67–22 for abusing members of the committee investigating him. The term "[[McCarthyism|McCarthyism]]" came to describe the anti-communist Red Scare as a whole, and later any reckless and unsubstantiated accusation. He died of hepatitis, which some biographers say was linked to alcoholism.

English man with severe physical deformities. Born in [[Leicester|Leicester]], Merrick was exhibited at freak shows as "The Elephant Man" before surgeon Frederick Treves invited him to the London Hospital, where he lived for the rest of his life. He created detailed artistic works, such as model buildings, and became well known in London society. He died in the hospital; the official cause was asphyxia, but Treves concluded that he had died of a dislocated neck. His life was depicted in a 1977 play and in a 1980 film by David Lynch, both titled *The Elephant Man*.

English chemist and Unitarian theologian. Priestley isolated [[Oxygen|oxygen]] in 1774, calling it "dephlogisticated air", and also invented carbonated water and wrote on electricity. He defended the phlogiston theory, which left him isolated as the chemical revolution advanced. Advocating toleration for religious Dissenters, he helped found [[Unitarianism|Unitarianism]] in England. He supported the [[American Revolution|American Revolution]] and the [[French Revolution|French Revolution]]; after a mob burned his home and church in [[Birmingham|Birmingham]], he fled to London and then to the United States. His educational works included a seminal English grammar, and his metaphysical writings were considered primary sources for [[Utilitarianism|utilitarianism]]. He published over 150 works.

Hungarian-born American newspaper publisher and politician. He published the St. Louis Post-Dispatch and the New York World and was a leading figure in the U.S. Democratic Party, serving one term in Congress. In the 1890s his competition with William Randolph Hearst's New York Journal helped develop yellow journalism, and the World's circulation reached a million copies a day. Pulitzer had enlisted in the Union Army during the [[American Civil War|American Civil War]]. His bequest to [[Columbia University|Columbia University]] established the [[Pulitzer Prize|Pulitzer Prizes]] in 1917, awarded annually for journalism, literature, history, music and drama. He also funded the Columbia School of Journalism, which opened in 1912.

American founder of the Latter Day Saint movement. Born in [[Vermont|Vermont]], Smith said that an angel revealed buried golden plates to him, and in 1830 he published the Book of Mormon as their English translation. The same year he organized the Church of Christ, whose members became known as Latter Day Saints or Mormons. The church that succeeded it, [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints|the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]], is the largest of its denominations. He led followers through Kirtland, Independence and Nauvoo, [[Illinois|Illinois]], where he was city mayor. He practiced [[Polygamy|polygamy]], and the 1844 destruction of a newspaper critical of it inflamed opposition. He was shot by a mob at a jail in Carthage. Mormons regard him as a prophet comparable to [[Moses|Moses]] and [[Elijah|Elijah]].

American-born French dancer, singer and actress, and a spy for the French Resistance. She was the first Black woman to star in a major motion picture, the 1927 French silent film *Siren of the Tropics*. Her performances in the Folies Bergère revues in [[Paris|Paris]] made her banana-skirt costume an iconic symbol of the Jazz Age and the [[Roaring Twenties|Roaring Twenties]]. She became a French national after marrying Jean Lion in 1937 and aided the French Resistance during World War II, earning the Croix de Guerre. [[Charles de Gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]] named her a Knight of the Legion of Honour. She refused to perform for segregated audiences in the United States and contributed to the [[Civil rights movement|civil rights movement]]. She adopted twelve children, the "Rainbow Tribe".

Roman–Jewish historian and military leader. Born in [[Jerusalem|Jerusalem]] to a priestly father and a mother who claimed Hasmonean royal ancestry, he commanded Jewish forces in Galilee at the start of the First Jewish–Roman War. He surrendered to Vespasian in AD 67 and, after Vespasian became emperor, was freed and took the family name Flavius. As Titus's translator he served during the siege of Jerusalem in AD 70. His works include *The Jewish War*, *Antiquities of the Jews* and an autobiography. They give extra-biblical accounts of [[Pontius Pilate|Pontius Pilate]], [[Herod the Great|Herod the Great]], [[John the Baptist|John the Baptist]] and Jesus of Nazareth, and are a chief source next to the Bible for ancient Israel and Judea.

English potter, entrepreneur and abolitionist, founder of the Wedgwood company in 1759. He developed improved pottery bodies by systematic experimentation and led the [[Industrial Revolution|industrialization]] of European pottery manufacture. The company never made [[Porcelain|porcelain]] in his lifetime but produced fine earthenwares such as creamware, black basalt and jasperware, and was an early adopter of transfer printing. He is credited as a pioneer of modern [[Marketing|marketing]], using direct mail, money-back guarantees, self-service, free delivery and illustrated catalogs. Each new invention, including green glaze, creamware, black basalt and jasperware, was quickly copied. He commissioned the "Am I Not a Man and a Brother?" anti-slavery medallion. He was the grandfather of Charles and Emma Darwin.

American scientist and mechanical engineer. His work on the applications of [[Thermodynamics|thermodynamics]] helped turn [[Physical chemistry|physical chemistry]] into a rigorous deductive science. With [[James Clerk Maxwell|James Clerk Maxwell]] and [[Ludwig Boltzmann|Ludwig Boltzmann]], he created [[Statistical mechanics|statistical mechanics]], a term he coined. He also created modern [[Vector calculus|vector calculus]] and described the Gibbs phenomenon in Fourier analysis. In 1863 Yale awarded him the first American doctorate in engineering, and he became professor of mathematical physics at [[Yale University|Yale]] in 1871. In 1901 he received the Copley Medal. [[Albert Einstein|Albert Einstein]] praised him as "the greatest mind in American history".

Yugoslav communist leader, prime minister (1943–1963) and president (1953–1980). Born Josip Broz, he led the Partisans, the Yugoslav guerrilla movement, during World War II; by the end of 1943 they had taken power with Allied backing. He defied [[Joseph Stalin|Joseph Stalin]], and Yugoslavia was expelled from the Cominform in 1948 in the Tito–Stalin split. He co-founded the [[Non-Aligned Movement|Non-Aligned Movement]] and, with Edvard Kardelj and Milovan Đilas, developed socialist self-management. His constitution delegated much power to the republics of the [[Yugoslavia|Yugoslav]] federation. A [[Cult of personality|cult of personality]] arose around him. Historians disagree on whether his presidency was authoritarian or that of a benevolent dictator. He received 98 foreign decorations.

Franco-Flemish composer of Renaissance music. Considered one of the greatest composers of the Renaissance, he was a central figure of the Franco-Flemish School. He developed expressive, imitative [[Renaissance music|polyphony]] that emphasized the relationship between text and music, using shorter, repeated motifs between voices. His compositions are mainly vocal, including masses, motets and secular chansons. He served several popes and the courts of Louis XII and Ercole I d'Este. He is described as the first Western composer to retain posthumous fame, and Martin Luther praised him. In the Baroque era he was overshadowed by [[Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina|Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina]]; a 1971 academic conference prompted his reevaluation.

American filmmaker, comic book writer and composer. He created the television series [[Buffy the Vampire Slayer|Buffy the Vampire Slayer]] and its spinoff *Angel*, as well as *Firefly* and *Dollhouse*. He co-wrote the [[Pixar|Pixar]] film *Toy Story* (1995). For the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel Cinematic Universe]] he wrote and directed *The Avengers* (2012) and *Avengers: Age of Ultron* (2015). He wrote and directed *Serenity* (2005) and *Much Ado About Nothing* (2012). Since 2020, several actors, producers and writers have accused him of creating toxic workplaces. Whedon has denied any wrongdoing, while acknowledging that he can be "confrontational".

Unit of energy in the [[International System of Units|International System of Units]] (SI), symbol J. One joule is the work done when a force of one [[Newton (unit)|newton]] moves a body one meter in the direction of the force. It is also the energy dissipated as [[Heat|heat]] when an electric current of one ampere passes through a resistance of one [[Ohm|ohm]] for one second. In SI base units it equals one kilogram-meter squared per second squared (kg⋅m²⋅s⁻²). It is named after the English physicist [[James Prescott Joule|James Prescott Joule]]; Wilhelm Siemens first proposed the name in 1882, and it was officially adopted in 1889. One joule equals one watt-second or one [[Coulomb|coulomb]]-[[Volt|volt]], and a kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 megajoules. The 1948 General Conference on Weights and Measures preferred the joule as the unit of heat in calorimetry, officially deprecating the calorie.

American rock band formed in [[San Francisco|San Francisco]] in 1973. Its greatest commercial success came between 1978 and 1987, when Steve Perry was lead vocalist. The album *Escape* reached number one on the Billboard 200, and "Don't Stop Believin'" (1981) is certified 18-times platinum by the RIAA. Filipino vocalist Arnel Pineda joined in 2007 after being discovered on [[YouTube|YouTube]]. The band has been inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and has released 25 gold and platinum albums. Originally a progressive rock band, it embraced pop arrangements by 1978 on the album *Infinity*.
